q: What must a linear axis do to organize a spatial composition?
o: Act as a continuous line/plane linking scattered elements
An imaginary line with length and direction needing terminating elements at both ends
Balance visual mass around a virtual center
It functions as a continuous line, plane, or volume that draws together, accumulates, and stabilizes separate elements through its structural and visual continuity.
n: Ching: an axis is an imaginary line of length and direction that requires terminating elements at both ends to anchor its visual force.

q: How does a datum bring order to varied forms and spaces?
o: By acting as a continuous line, plane, or volume that gathers and organizes elements
An imaginary line needing terminating elements
Balancing visual mass around a center
It works as an unbroken line, plane, or volume that draws together, accumulates, and stabilizes separate elements through its structural and visual continuity.
n: Ching: a datum is a continuous line, plane, or volume whose regularity gathers and organizes a scattered set of forms.

q: Which is NOT one of the three ways an element achieves hierarchical dominance?
n: Ching's three ways an element achieves hierarchical dominance are by size, shape, and strategic placement --- concealment is the opposite of dominance.

q: What turns simple repetition into architectural rhythm?
o: Arranging elements on a curved plane
Forming a structured/alternating sequence guiding the eye
n: Simple repetition becomes rhythm only when the repeated elements form a structured or alternating sequence that guides the eye.

q: What is the goal of 'Transformation' in design morphology?
o: Changing a shape step-by-step until unrecognizable
Modifying a form through geometric changes while keeping its grid/identity
Altering a form until it loses its identity
Making interiors disorient viewers from outside
n: Transformation is the incremental alteration of a form while its underlying grid/identity remains recognizable, per Ching's design vocabulary.

q: How can an asymmetrical composition still achieve balance?
o: Light mass near center, heavy mass far out
A heavy element near center balanced by a light element far from center
Large mass near center with light elements removed
n: Asymmetrical balance works like a lever: a small mass far from the center can balance a large mass near it.

q: How does transformation help when adding a modern wing to a historic library?
o: Studying the old grid/proportions and applying those rules to the new design
Improving old structural bays, then repurposing the library
Requiring the new wing to be an exact replica
n: In adaptive reuse, architects study the historic grid, rhythm, and proportion of the old structure and extend those same rules into the new design.

q: Which configuration shows Radial Symmetry?
o: A circular altar with identical piers radiating outward
A long hospital wing with rooms on both sides
A skyscraper that twists as it rises
n: Radial symmetry is a central element with identical parts repeating outward around it, as in a circular altar with radiating piers.

q: What is the key difference between Proportion and Scale?
o: Proportion compares to a person; scale is part-to-whole
Proportion needs metric units, scale needs imperial
Proportion is part-to-part/whole relation; scale compares to an external standard
Scale is set by engineers, proportion by clients
n: Proportion is the relationship of parts to each other and the whole; scale compares an object's size to an external reference, usually the human body.

q: In Classical Orders, what module derives all column and entablature dimensions?
o: The height of the entrance portal
The base diameter of the column shaft
A dimension chosen arbitrarily by the mason
n: In the Classical Orders, the module is the base diameter of the column shaft, from which all other dimensions are derived.

q: What belief drove Renaissance architects like Palladio to base proportions on musical ratios?
o: Deep walls were needed to amplify music
Musical ratios reflected a cosmic order applicable to space
Applying the mathematical ratios of musical harmony to building dimensions to reflect a divine order.
Ratios were used to confuse rival builders
n: Renaissance theorists like Palladio believed musical harmonic ratios reflected a divine, cosmic order and translated those ratios directly into building proportions.

q: What does 'Anthropometry' primarily study as a proportioning system?
o: Human body dimensions, reach, and clearance needs
n: Anthropometry is the study of human body dimensions, reach, and clearance requirements used to size architectural elements.

q: The Fibonacci sequence is linked to which proportioning system?
n: The Fibonacci sequence approximates the Golden Ratio, the basis of the Golden Section proportioning system.

q: What is Le Corbusier's universal scaling system based on the Golden Ratio and human proportions called?
n: Le Corbusier's Modulor combined the Golden Ratio with human body proportions into a universal scale.

q: Which Vitruvian triad term represents function and efficient program arrangement?
n: In the Vitruvian triad, Utilitas refers to function/utility, Firmitas to structure, and Venustas to beauty.

q: What spatial relationship occurs when a larger space fully encloses a smaller one?
o: Spaces linked by a common space
n: 'Space within a space' occurs when a larger volume fully contains and encloses a smaller one.

q: Which layout has a dominant central space with arms extending outward like spokes?
n: Radial organization extends linear arms outward from a dominant central space, like spokes on a wheel.

q: Which organizing system uses a repeating 3D matrix of bays to regulate layout?
n: Grid organization uses a repeating three-dimensional matrix of bays to regulate form and layout.

q: What term, coined by Edward T. Hall, studies culturally determined spatial distances between people?
n: Edward T. Hall coined 'proxemics' for the study of culturally determined personal spatial distances.

q: Which proxemic zone (about 1.5-4 ft) is reserved for close friends and family?
n: Hall's Personal Distance zone (about 1.5--4 ft) is reserved for close friends and family.

q: Which Japanese module governs both column layout and tatami mat sizing?
n: The Ken is a Japanese modular unit that governs both the structural column grid and standard tatami mat sizes.

q: What term describes a beam/slab projecting past its support, held by internal tension?
n: A cantilever is a horizontal member that projects beyond its support, held by internal tension/counterbalance rather than an end support.

q: What principle harmonizes all elements of a composition so nothing distracts from the concept?
n: Unity is achieved when all compositional elements are harmonized around one overarching concept, with nothing distracting from it.

q: What kind of rhythm results from a gradual, step-by-step change in an element's size/shape?
n: Progressive rhythm is created by a step-by-step, predictable change in an element's size, shape, or spacing.

q: Which scale intentionally makes people feel small to project institutional power?
n: Monumental scale intentionally overwhelms the individual to project institutional, state, or religious power.

q: Which design element marks a position with no dimension and generates all other forms?
n: A point marks a position in space with no dimension, and is the primitive generator of line, plane, and volume.

q: What term describes a form's degree of stability based on shape, orientation, and ground relation?
n: Visual inertia describes a form's degree of stability/concentration, based on its shape, orientation, and relation to the ground.

q: What transformation type removes volume from a form while keeping its overall identity?
n: Removing volume from a primary solid while its overall identity remains recognizable is a subtractive transformation.

q: What effect does an elevated base plane have relative to surrounding ground?
n: An elevated plane visually and psychologically separates itself, creating a sense of prominence, detachment, and territory.

q: What effect does a depressed base plane have relative to surrounding ground?
n: A depressed plane forms an introverted, sheltered field of space distinct from --- but continuous with --- the surrounding ground.

q: What term describes the outline/contour that lets us identify a form?
n: Shape is the characteristic outline/contour that lets us identify and distinguish a form.

q: Rotating a triangle about its vertical apex axis generates which volume?
n: Rotating a triangle about its vertical apex axis sweeps out a cone.

q: What term describes a place's unique character rooted in geography, history, and form ('spirit of place')?
n: 'Genius loci,' Latin for 'spirit of place,' describes the unique character rooted in a site's geography, history, and form.

q: How does a polished, reflective floor alter perception of a lobby?
o: Makes it feel dark and cramped
Mirrors the ceiling, creating an illusion of extra height
n: A polished reflective floor mirrors the ceiling plane, creating an illusion of greater vertical height.

q: How is a 'Tone' produced in color theory?
n: In color theory a tone is produced by adding grey (a mix of black and white) to a pure hue.

q: What term describes a hue mixed with black, making it darker?
n: A shade is a hue mixed with black, which lowers its value and darkens it.

q: Which color is clinically linked to lowering blood pressure and creating a calm healing environment?
n: Low-chroma/desaturated blue is documented to calm the nervous system, lowering blood pressure and respiration --- useful in healing environments.

q: In a split-complementary scheme based on Yellow, what two colors balance it?
n: Yellow's complement is violet; a split-complementary scheme pairs yellow with the two hues flanking violet --- red-violet and blue-violet.

q: What color harmony pairs hues directly opposite on the color wheel?
n: Complementary harmony pairs hues directly opposite each other on the color wheel.

q: In commercial kitchen design, what layout links the sink, fridge, and range for efficiency?
n: The Work Triangle links the sink, refrigerator, and range/stove for efficient kitchen circulation.

q: What clearance is needed between facing kitchen equipment rows for staff to pass back-to-back with oven doors open?
n: Commercial kitchen guidelines call for roughly 1500 mm between facing equipment rows when staff must pass back-to-back with oven doors open.

q: What is the minimum width for a secondary residential corridor to let two people pass comfortably?
n: Building/space-planning standards set about 1200 mm as the minimum secondary corridor width for two people to pass comfortably.

q: What is the key conceptual difference between 'Personal Space' and 'Territoriality'?
o: Personal space needs legal ownership, territoriality doesn't
Personal space is interior-only, territoriality is urban-only
Personal space is fixed, territoriality is mobile
Personal space is a portable bubble; territoriality is a fixed claimed area
n: Personal space is a portable psychological 'bubble' that travels with a person, while territoriality is a fixed area someone claims and defends.

q: Which of Alan Westin's privacy states describes being unidentified while present in a public crowd?
n: Alan Westin's 'anonymity' describes being unidentified and unobserved while present in a public crowd.

q: Why do accessibility codes require high-contrast colors between doors, signage, and walls?
o: To absorb noise on evacuation routes
To guide low-vision users to paths of travel and exits
n: High-contrast signage/door colors under codes like BP 344 help low-vision users identify paths of travel and exits.

q: How can color selection influence thermal comfort in workspaces?
o: Cool colors lower perceived temperature in hot climates
Color has no effect on temperature perception
n: Cool colors (blues/greens) can lower a room's perceived temperature, helping thermal comfort in hot climates.

q: What color approach suits a fast-casual restaurant aiming for quick turnover?
o: High-saturation colors to stimulate appetite and mild restlessness
Low-saturation colors for the same effect
n: High-saturation warm colors stimulate appetite while producing mild restlessness, encouraging quick turnover in fast-casual dining.

q: What structural shift marks the transition from Old Kingdom to New Kingdom Egyptian royal tombs?
o: Visible pyramids to hidden rock-cut tombs to deter raiders
n: Egyptian royal burials shifted from visible Old Kingdom pyramids to hidden, rock-cut New Kingdom tombs (Valley of the Kings) to deter raiders.

q: What technological breakthrough enabled the shift from Greek to Roman structural design?
o: Concrete (opus caementicium) and the true arch replacing trabeation
n: Rome's development of opus caementicium (concrete) and the true arch freed architecture from the strictly post-and-lintel Greek trabeated system.

q: Why is the 1851 Crystal Palace (Great Exhibition, London) a watershed moment?
o: First public building with hand-carved marble orders
It ended urban planning regulation in Europe
It proved rapid construction using prefabricated iron and glass
It introduced the first electric elevator
n: The Crystal Palace proved that a massive building could be rapidly assembled from prefabricated, modular iron-and-glass components.

q: Arrange these design movements in correct chronological order.
o: Gothic → Baroque → Renaissance → Art Nouveau → Modernism
Gothic → Renaissance → Baroque → Art Nouveau → Modernism
Renaissance → Gothic → Baroque → Modernism → Art Nouveau
Baroque → Gothic → Renaissance → Modernism → Art Nouveau
n: The correct historical order is Gothic → Renaissance → Baroque → Art Nouveau → Modernism.

q: What element did Sullivan use to express a skyscraper's tripartite division, like a classical column?
o: An uninterrupted glass facade exposing the core
Buttresses that thin as the building rises
n: Sullivan described the skyscraper's tripartite division --- base, shaft, and cornice/top --- echoing a classical column.

q: What structural element unlocks the 'free plan' and 'free facade' in Le Corbusier's Five Points?
o: Pilotis with an internal column grid and cantilevered slabs
n: Pilotis, an internal reinforced-concrete column grid, and cantilevered slabs free both the plan and facade from load-bearing walls.

q: How is 'Organic Architecture' implemented in Wright's Fallingwater?
o: Concrete terraces blended into the site, mimicking rock ledges
A circular plan avoiding right angles
n: Fallingwater's cantilevered concrete terraces echo the natural rock ledges of the site, embodying Wright's organic architecture.

q: What strategy did Gropius use to emphasize weightlessness in the Bauhaus Dessau workshop wing?
o: A continuous glass curtain wall independent of the recessed structural grid
Thick brick walls with small windows
Tensile fabric and steel cable structure
n: Gropius wrapped the Dessau workshop wing in a continuous glass curtain wall set free of the recessed structural grid, expressing weightlessness.

q: How did Mies express structure on the Seagram Building's exterior while meeting fire codes?
o: Leaving structural steel exposed without fireproofing
Applying non-structural bronze I-beam mullions over fireproofed steel
A structural glass fin system with no mullions
An exterior cast entirely of raw concrete
n: Fire codes required Mies to fireproof the Seagram Building's real steel frame, so he applied non-structural bronze I-beam mullions to express structural rhythm.

q: How did Aalto integrate humanistic factors into the Paimio Sanatorium design?
o: Custom glare-free lighting, curved sinks, and soothing colors for patients
n: Aalto tailored Paimio Sanatorium's fixtures, sinks, and colors specifically to the psychological and physical needs of bedridden patients.

q: In which book did Venturi argue for embracing complexity and contradiction over modernist purism?
n: Venturi's 1966 book 'Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture' argued for embracing ambiguity over modernist purism.

q: What defines the High-Tech style of the Pompidou Center?
o: Exposing and color-coding structural and MEP systems on the exterior
n: The Pompidou Center exposes and color-codes its structural and MEP systems on the exterior, the hallmark of High-Tech design.

q: Which fragmented, titanium-clad project brought Deconstructivism to global prominence?
o: Parc de la Villette by Tschumi
n: Gehry's titanium-clad, fragmented Guggenheim Bilbao brought Deconstructivism to mainstream global attention.

q: What material reality gave rise to the term 'Brutalism' at Unité d'Habitation?
o: Raw exposed steel left to rust
Rough concrete left raw from formwork ('béton brut')
n: 'Brutalism' derives from 'béton brut' --- raw concrete left exposed as cast, seen at Le Corbusier's Unité d'Habitation.

q: How did Niemeyer's Brasília works depart from European functionalism?
o: Sculptural reinforced concrete curves inspired by Brazil's geography
n: Niemeyer's Brasília works used sculptural, curving reinforced concrete inspired by Brazil's landscape, diverging from rigid European functionalism.

q: What is the spatial goal of Hadid's undulating skin at the Heydar Aliyev Center?
o: A fluid design where the plaza folds upward into walls and roof
n: Hadid's Heydar Aliyev Center dissolves the ground/building boundary, letting the plaza fold upward to become walls and roof.

q: What is a key spatial/contextual difference between the Glass House and Farnsworth House?
o: Glass House on stilts over a floodplain, Farnsworth flat on concrete
Glass House sits on the ground with a brick core, Farnsworth is elevated on steel columns
Farnsworth is opaque timber, Glass House is transparent
Glass House uses stone arches, Farnsworth uses a steel space frame
n: The Glass House sits on the ground with a solid brick core, while the Farnsworth House is elevated on steel columns above the floodplain.

q: How did Japanese Metabolism (e.g. Kurokawa) conceptualize buildings?
o: As organisms with a fixed spine and replaceable plug-in units
As mobile vehicles on mechanical tracks
n: Metabolism envisioned buildings as organisms with a fixed structural core and replaceable, plug-in capsule/module units.

q: Which Five Points element creates Villa Savoye's elevated open-air living space?
n: The Roof Garden is the Five Points element that creates Villa Savoye's open-air living space on the upper level.

q: What defines the focal point of Ando's Church of the Light interior?
o: A cruciform void cut into the concrete wall to admit light
n: Tadao Ando cuts a cruciform void into the raw concrete altar wall of the Church of the Light to admit natural light.

q: Who curated MoMA's 1932 exhibition that defined the International Style?
n: Henry-Russell Hitchcock and Philip Johnson curated MoMA's 1932 exhibition that named and defined the International Style.

q: What apex detail of the AT&T Building sparked debate as a Postmodern icon?
o: A broken pediment resembling Chippendale furniture
A functional orange exterior elevator cage
n: The AT&T Building's open, broken pediment resembling Chippendale furniture became the most debated Postmodern gesture of its time.

q: What geometric breakthrough let Utzon and Ove Arup fabricate the Sydney Opera House shells?
o: Every shell segment could be cut from one common sphere's surface
Shells built from canvas over steel frames
Using AI to generate random forms
n: Utzon and Ove Arup discovered every Sydney Opera House shell could be cut from the surface of one common sphere, enabling standardized fabrication.

q: What is the symbolic/geometric basis of Libeskind's zigzag plan at the Jewish Museum Berlin?
o: A transcription of a symphony's sound wave
A distorted Star of David linked to Berlin addresses, cut by a void
n: Libeskind's zigzag plan derives from a distorted Star of David linking Berlin addresses, cut through by a linear void of absence.

q: How did Mies achieve fluid open space at the Barcelona Pavilion?
o: Slender cruciform steel columns carrying loads, freeing stone/glass planes to float independently
n: Slender cruciform steel columns carry all structural load in the Barcelona Pavilion, freeing the stone and glass planes to float independently.

q: Who formulated the Modulor, an anthropometric scale based on the human body and Golden Ratio?
n: Le Corbusier devised the Modulor, an anthropometric scale based on human proportions and the Golden Ratio.

q: What led to the Nakagin Capsule Tower's 2022 demolition?
o: Lack of a concrete core causing lean
Decay from unreplaced capsules, rusted joints, burst pipes, and asbestos
n: The Nakagin Capsule Tower was demolished after decades of unreplaced capsules led to rusted joints, burst pipes, and asbestos hazards.

q: What imagery did Saarinen evoke with the TWA Flight Center's shell vaults?
o: A bird or airplane in flight, capturing jet-age optimism
n: Saarinen shaped the TWA Flight Center's thin-shell vaults to evoke a bird or airplane in flight, capturing jet-age optimism.

q: What facade detail of the Vanna Venturi House subverts Modernist functionalism?
o: A transparent curtain wall exposing bedrooms
An oversized non-structural gable with a split lintel and applied molding
A steel column in the driveway
n: The Vanna Venturi House's oversized, non-structural gable with a split lintel and applied molding mocks Modernist functionalist honesty.

q: What breakthrough did Shigeru Ban's use of cardboard tubes enable?
o: Fast, low-cost disaster-relief housing for refugees/victims
n: Shigeru Ban's paper/cardboard-tube structures enabled fast, low-cost disaster-relief shelters for refugees and disaster victims.

q: How did Art Nouveau structurally integrate organic ornament, per Horta's Hôtel Tassel?
o: Iron/steel sculpted into biomorphic curves, blending structure and decoration
n: Victor Horta's Hôtel Tassel fused Art Nouveau ornament directly into structural iron and steel, sculpted into biomorphic curves.

q: How did 1916 NYC zoning shape Art Deco skyscrapers like the Chrysler Building?
o: Setback rules based on a 'sky exposure plane' creating a 'wedding cake' form
Banning steel above the tenth floor
n: NYC's 1916 zoning law required setbacks along a 'sky exposure plane,' producing the tiered 'wedding cake' Art Deco skyscraper profile.

q: What tension defines the Einstein Tower's construction reality?
o: Rigid machine look built from timber logs
Meant to look like fluid concrete but built in brick/stucco due to shortages
n: Material shortages forced Mendelsohn's Einstein Tower to be built in brick and stucco rather than the fluid poured concrete he intended.

q: What three criteria defined the International Style per Hitchcock and Johnson?
o: Volume over mass, regularity over symmetry, rejection of ornament
n: Hitchcock and Johnson's three criteria were volume over mass, regularity over axial symmetry, and rejection of applied ornament.

q: How does the Ronchamp Chapel challenge Corbusier's earlier functionalist work?
o: It keeps a rigid right-angled column-and-slab system
It replaces concrete with timber framing
It uses mass-produced glass panels on steel grids
It abandons the white-cube geometry for irregular openings, heavy walls, and a curved roof
n: Ronchamp abandons Corbusier's earlier white-cube rationalism for irregular window punctures, thick sculptural walls, and a curved crab-shell roof.

q: What theoretical shift marked the Bauhaus move from Weimar to Dessau?
o: From craftsmanship to industrial standardization/mass production
Abandoning steel for Roman stone arches
n: The Bauhaus's move to Dessau reflected Gropius's turn from individual craft toward industrial standardization and mass production.

q: How does the Portland Building's facade break from the International Style?
o: Classical tripartite division with polychrome graphics, oversized pilasters, and a ribbon
A fully transparent columnless glass skin
n: Graves' Portland Building reintroduces a classical tripartite facade with polychrome graphics, oversized pilasters, and a decorative ribbon.

q: What defines a 'Decorated Shed' per Venturi, Scott Brown, and Izenour?
o: A structural form deformed into a literal sculptural sign
A plain functional building with applied signs to convey meaning
A structure with dynamic kinetic geometry
n: Venturi, Scott Brown, and Izenour defined a 'Decorated Shed' as a plain functional building carrying applied signs/ornament to communicate meaning.

q: What structural method underlies Safdie's Habitat 67?
o: A single wall dividing the complex
354 stacked prefabricated concrete boxes in a terraced layout
Living spaces sunk into limestone shafts
n: Habitat 67 stacks 354 prefabricated concrete housing modules in an irregular, terraced arrangement.

q: What structural system carries the HSBC HQ's floors?
o: Exterior steel masts and suspension trusses freeing the interior of columns
n: The HSBC HQ hangs its floors from exterior steel masts and suspension trusses, freeing the interior of columns.

q: What engineering technique gives Calatrava's Milwaukee Art Museum addition its biomorphic form?
o: An operable Burke Brise Soleil controlling solar gain
n: Calatrava's Milwaukee Art Museum addition uses the operable Burke Brise Soleil, a movable sunshade 'wing', to control solar gain.

q: How does the shift from Modernist linearity to Parametric fluidity reflect architecture's evolution?
o: Limiting podium heights to ten stories
Shifting from CAD to AI language for design
A shift from industrial standardization to flexible, computer-guided, context-responsive systems
n: The shift to Parametricism reflects a move from standardized industrial forms toward flexible, computer-guided, context-responsive design.

q: What is the mechanical purpose of Paoay Church's massive 'Earthquake Baroque' buttresses?
o: Maximizing floor area by moving supports outside
Resisting lateral seismic forces by transferring loads diagonally to ground
n: The Earthquake Baroque buttresses of Paoay Church resist lateral seismic forces, channeling loads diagonally down to the ground.

q: Which Juan Arellano building is a Philippine Art Deco masterpiece with native floral motifs?
n: Juan Arellano's Manila Metropolitan Theater is the landmark Philippine Art Deco building with stylized native floral motifs.

q: What design shift is evident in Juan Nakpil's mid-century civic works like the SSS Building?
o: Structural expressionism and clean geometric corporate lines
n: Nakpil's postwar civic works, like the SSS Building, moved toward structural expressionism and clean corporate geometry.

q: Why did colonial architects like Antonio Toledo use Neoclassical style for public buildings?
o: To project democratic authority and institutional stability through monumental symmetry
n: Neoclassicism's monumental columns and symmetry were used on colonial civic buildings to project democratic authority and institutional stability.

q: What did Tomas Mapua's transition to professionalized practice primarily mean?
o: Moving away from codes toward hand-drawn craft
Institutionalizing formal engineering, testing, and academic training
Standardizing civic/residential designs for the country
n: Mapua's practice reflected the shift toward formal engineering calculation, material testing, and academic training in Philippine architecture.

q: What passive cooling technique did Pablo Antonio prioritize at Far Eastern University?
o: Wide corridors, large windows, and orientation for cross-ventilation
Stack ventilation sweeping cool air across floors
Shaded arcades and verandas with concrete for durability
n: Pablo Antonio's FEU campus uses wide corridors, expansive windows, and orientation to maximize natural cross-ventilation.

q: How did Carlos Arguelles modify the International Style curtain wall for the Philamlife Building?
o: Made the envelope airtight and placed it underground
n: Carlos Arguelles adapted the International Style curtain wall for Manila's climate with exterior aluminum sun-shading louvers.

q: What effect does Locsin's cantilevered concrete block over a glass base create at the CCP?
o: Directs compression down a shell curve, removing need for columns
An illusion of a massive concrete volume floating
Shows thin glass can carry concrete floors
n: Locsin's cantilevered CCP theater block creates a striking illusion of a massive concrete volume floating above the glass base.

q: How does the San Miguel Corporation Building's stepped geometry function environmentally?
o: Blending modern forms with classical hierarchy for spiritual scale
Enabling a column-free interior with minimal material
Self-shading floors and landscaping to cut solar heat gain
Shaded arcades and durable concrete for storms
n: The Mañosa brothers' terraced San Miguel building self-shades its floors and integrates landscaping to cut solar heat gain.

q: What theoretical approach do Jose Maria Zaragoza's church designs (e.g. Santo Domingo) demonstrate?
o: Blending modern structural forms with classical hierarchy for spiritual scale
A column-free layout maximizing altar sightlines
Shaded arcades and durable concrete construction
n: Zaragoza's Santo Domingo Church blends modern structural forms with classical spatial hierarchy to evoke spiritual scale.

q: What was a key element of William Parsons's tropical adaptation of reinforced concrete at the Manila Hotel?
o: Blending modern forms with classical hierarchy
A column-free layout for altar sightlines
Shaded arcades, deep verandas, and high ceilings using durable concrete
n: Parsons adapted Manila Hotel's concrete construction to the tropics with shaded arcades, deep verandas, and high ceilings.

q: What advantage did the thin-shell dome of Church of the Holy Sacrifice (UP Diliman) offer?
o: Blending modern forms with classical hierarchy
A column-free interior maximizing altar sightlines
Shaded arcades and durable concrete construction
n: The Church of the Holy Sacrifice's thin-shell dome eliminates interior columns, opening sightlines toward the central altar.

q: What macroclimate classification describes the Philippine archipelago?
n: The Philippines' overall climate classification is Maritime Tropical.

q: What wind blows from the Northeast bringing cool, dry air from Nov-Feb?
n: The Amihan is the cool, dry northeast wind that dominates the Philippines from roughly November to February.

q: What wind blows from the Southwest bringing moist monsoon air from June-Oct?
n: The Habagat is the moist southwest monsoon wind that dominates from about June to October.

q: Why does high humidity make a space feel hotter than the thermometer reading?
o: Stops sweat from evaporating, trapping body heat
n: High humidity slows sweat evaporation, trapping body heat and making the same temperature feel hotter.

q: What term describes dense cities like Manila running 2-5°C warmer than rural areas?
n: The Urban Heat Island Effect describes dense cities running measurably warmer than surrounding rural land due to dark, hard surfaces.

q: What problem arises from a very small diurnal temperature range in the tropics?
o: Warm nights fail to flush heat trapped in concrete walls
n: A small diurnal range means nights don't cool enough to flush the solar heat that concrete/masonry walls absorbed during the day.

q: What term describes cool ocean air moving inland in the afternoon as land air rises?
n: A sea breeze is the daily cycle where cooler ocean air moves inland in the afternoon as land air heats and rises.

q: Which axis orientation best keeps a building cool by avoiding direct sun on its long walls?
n: Stretching a building's long axis East-to-West minimizes the exposed wall area facing the intense low-angle morning/afternoon sun.

q: Which facades get the most intense low-angle sun, hard to shade with horizontal overhangs?
n: East and West facades receive intense, low-angle sun that horizontal overhangs (better suited to high-angle sun) can't easily block.

q: Which shading device best blocks high-angle noon sun on North/South facades?
n: Deep horizontal overhangs/canopies are most effective at blocking the high-angle noon sun typical on North/South facades.

q: Which shading device best blocks low-angle morning/afternoon sun on East/West facades?
n: Vertical louvers or fins are best suited to block the low, raking morning/afternoon sun on East/West facades.

q: What happens at night with an unshaded concrete roof slab in the tropics?
o: It turns instantly cold causing condensation
Stored daytime heat radiates downward at night
n: A massive unshaded concrete roof stores solar heat during the day and re-radiates it downward into the interior at night.

q: What roof pitch sheds monsoon rain fast while venting hot air away from occupants?
o: Mono-sloped roof toward the windward inlet
n: A steep roof pitch with generous eaves sheds heavy monsoon rain fast while letting hot air rise and pool near the peak, away from occupants.

q: What is the function of a breeze block screen wall in tropical buildings?
o: Reduce glare while letting air pass through
n: Breeze blocks perforate a wall to cut direct glare while still letting natural airflow pass through.

q: What does 'Azimuth' represent in solar geometry?
o: The sun's horizontal angular position along the horizon
n: Azimuth is the sun's horizontal angular position measured along the horizon; altitude is its vertical angle.

q: What U-value should wall insulation have to minimize heat transfer?
o: Low, indicating high resistance to heat flow
n: Good insulation should have a low U-value, meaning high resistance to heat flow.

q: Why should highly reflective finishes be used cautiously in dense neighborhoods?
o: They absorb heat into adjacent buildings
n: Highly reflective finishes can bounce intense solar glare and heat onto neighboring buildings and streets.

q: What principle explains air speeding up when forced through a narrow opening?
n: The Venturi Effect explains why air speeds up when forced through a narrowed opening.

q: What inlet/outlet sizing maximizes cross-ventilation velocity?
o: Inlet smaller than or equal to outlet
Inlet larger than or equal to outlet
Both openings at the same height
n: Sizing the inlet smaller than the outlet creates a pressure differential (like a nozzle) that speeds up indoor air movement.

q: What ventilation mechanism relies on warm air rising and exiting high vents, pulling cool air in low?
n: The stack effect relies on warm, buoyant air rising and exiting high vents, drawing cooler air in through low openings.

q: Which window type allows near-100% ventilation while shedding rain?
n: Jalousie windows open to nearly 100% of their area while their angled glass slats still shed rain.

q: What landscape feature placed upwind of an inlet cools incoming air?
o: An asphalt lot with no trees
A lawn with a water feature for evaporative cooling
n: A water feature or lawn placed upwind of an inlet cools incoming air through evaporative cooling.

q: What is the passive cooling benefit of wide overhanging verandas in tropical resorts?
o: Shading perimeter walls from sun while sheltering from rain
n: Wide overhanging verandas shade a building's perimeter walls from direct sun while sheltering them from rain.

q: What glass technology reduces SHGC without external shading?
n: Low-Emissivity, reflective double-glazed units reduce a window's solar heat gain coefficient without needing external shading.

q: What material choice keeps the Bahay Kubo from storing heat?
o: Lightweight, porous materials with low thermal mass
n: The Bahay Kubo's light, porous natural materials (bamboo, nipa) have low thermal mass, so the structure doesn't store heat.

q: Why is the Bahay Kubo's floor elevated on stilts?
o: To protect from flooding and pests
For a security vantage during tribal wars
To maximize roof rigidity in typhoons
To isolate the house from ventilation
n: Elevating the Bahay Kubo on stilts protects occupants and the structure from floodwater and ground pests.

q: What feature combines Bahay Kubo's lightweight logic with heavy stone in a Bahay na Bato?
o: Stone upper floor on a bamboo ground floor
A heavy masonry ground floor topped by a timber upper story
An envelope entirely of imported sheet metal
n: The Bahay na Bato pairs a heavy masonry ground floor with a lighter timber upper residential story.

q: What pierced wooden screen near the ceiling in a Bahay na Bato lets hot air circulate between rooms?
n: The calado is a pierced wooden screen near the ceiling that lets hot air circulate freely between rooms.

q: What is the purpose of the ventanilla sliding panels below windowsills in a Bahay na Bato?
o: Allowing low-level cross-ventilation across the floor
Letting hot air flow between rooms
n: Ventanilla sliding panels beneath the windowsill admit low-level cross-ventilation across the floor where occupants sit.

q: What is the primary advantage of translucent Capiz shells in Bahay na Bato windows?
o: Diffusing soft light while withstanding typhoon winds
n: Capiz shell panes diffuse soft interior light while remaining durable enough to withstand typhoon winds.

q: What do closely spaced contour lines on a site map indicate?
n: Closely spaced contour lines indicate a steep slope or cliff.

q: What does soil bearing capacity tell an architect?
o: How much water soil holds in storms
How much weight the soil can safely support
n: Soil bearing capacity tells an architect how much load the ground can safely carry before a foundation sinks.

q: What does a 'cut and fill' grading strategy aim to achieve?
n: Cut-and-fill grading balances excavated and needed soil on site, minimizing the cost of hauling material away or importing it.

q: What is a 'bioswale' in sustainable site planning?
o: A shallow planted ditch that captures, slows, and filters stormwater
n: A bioswale is a shallow, planted depression designed to capture, slow, and filter stormwater runoff.

q: What challenge does a 'high water table' pose to a design?
o: Makes excavation harder but is otherwise safe
n: A high water table means shallow groundwater, making basements especially prone to flooding and requiring waterproofing.

q: What distinguishes a 'vista' from a 'panorama' in site design?
o: A vista is a framed view, a panorama is wide and open in all directions
Vista is night-only, panorama is day-only
n: A vista is a framed, directed view (often along an axis), while a panorama is a wide, open view in all directions.

q: Why align parking lanes North-to-South rather than East-to-West?
o: Minimizes low-angle sun exposure, keeping cars cooler
Aligns with the Earth's magnetic core
Fits more cars in the lot
n: Orienting parking rows North--South limits how long parked cars sit exposed to the low, direct East/West sun, keeping them cooler.

q: Why are native plants preferred over exotic plants in sustainable landscaping?
o: They need far less water, fertilizer, and maintenance
They grow faster than exotic plants
They are immune to solar radiation
n: Native plants are adapted to local conditions and typically need far less water, fertilizer, and maintenance than exotic species.

q: What site element best blocks loud highway noise from a residential building?
o: An open lawn with a concrete fence
An earth berm with dense shrubs and trees
n: An earth berm combined with dense shrubs and trees is an effective passive barrier against highway traffic noise.

q: What is a 'microclimate' in site analysis?
o: A localized area whose climate differs notably from the surrounding region
A regional climate spanning hundreds of km
A specific small-site climate shaped by its own features
A weather forecast changing every five minutes
n: A microclimate is a localized area whose temperature, humidity, wind, or rainfall differs notably from the surrounding regional climate.

q: What is the primary purpose of a 'site inventory' early in a project?
o: Cataloging all existing physical site features
Choosing existing elements and their cost
n: A site inventory catalogs all existing physical features of a site as a baseline before design begins.

q: Why is removing mature trees from a sloped site hazardous?
o: Roots stabilize soil/absorb rain; removal raises erosion/landslide risk
It weakens soil bearing capacity directly
It drops the water table too fast
n: Mature tree roots stabilize slope soil and absorb rainwater; removing them raises the risk of erosion and landslides.

q: What is an 'earth berm' in landscape design?
o: A raised, intentional mound of soil
n: An earth berm is a raised, intentionally shaped mound of soil used for screening, shading, or noise control.

q: What is the design advantage of deciduous trees for shading a south facade?
o: Providing wildlife food/shelter and erosion control
Acting as windbreaks and privacy screens
Shading in summer, dropping leaves to let sun through in winter
n: Deciduous trees shade a south facade in summer heat and drop their leaves in winter, letting sunlight through when it's wanted.

q: What term describes a broad paved public walkway along a waterfront for leisurely walking?
n: An esplanade is a broad, paved public walkway along a waterfront meant for leisurely strolling.

q: What outdoor structure has an open timber frame, often vine-covered, framing a path or seating area?
n: A pergola is an open timber framework of posts and cross-beams, often planted with vines, that frames a path or shaded seating area.

q: What landscape element is a dense row of shrubs forming a living wall for boundaries/screening?
n: A hedge is a dense, continuous planted row that forms a living wall marking boundaries or screening views.

q: What distinguishes 'hardscape' from 'softscape'?
o: Hardscape is non-living, softscape is all plant material
Hardscape is living, softscape is non-living
Hardscape is by architects, softscape by engineers only
Hardscape is water systems, softscape is lighting
n: Hardscape refers to non-living built elements (paving, walls), while softscape refers to living plant materials.

q: What was the core layout of Ebenezer Howard's 1898 Garden City concept?
o: A car-focused grid with no parks
A factory complex with housing on roofs
Self-contained walkable towns surrounded by a greenbelt
n: Howard's Garden City model proposed self-contained, walkable towns encircled by a protective greenbelt.

q: What is the primary goal of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)?
o: Building highways for faster car travel
Clustering dense housing/offices/shops near transit hubs
Making development scattered and far from transit
n: Transit-Oriented Development clusters dense housing, offices, and retail within easy walking distance of transit hubs.

q: What does 'urban sprawl' describe?
n: Urban sprawl describes the uncontrolled, low-density, outward expansion of a city.

q: What layout does the 'New Urbanism' movement champion?
n: New Urbanism promotes walkable, human-scaled neighborhoods in place of car-dependent sprawl.

q: How does the Concentric Zone Model describe city growth?
o: Concentric rings radiating from a central business district
n: The Concentric Zone Model (Burgess) describes a city as a series of rings expanding outward from a central business district.

q: How does the Sector Model (Hoyt) map urban land use?
o: Pie-shaped wedges growing along transportation corridors
n: The Sector Model (Hoyt) describes land use radiating outward in pie-shaped wedges along transportation corridors.

q: What claim does the 'Multiple Nuclei Model' make about metropolitan growth?
o: Growth around several independent, specialized hubs
n: The Multiple Nuclei Model holds that cities grow around several independent, specialized focal points rather than one center.

q: What is 'gentrification' in an urban context?
o: Wealthier residents moving into a low-income area, raising costs and displacing residents
n: Gentrification is the influx of wealthier residents into a lower-income neighborhood, raising costs and often displacing the original community.

q: What defines a 'Mega-city'?
n: A megacity is a continuous metropolitan area with a population exceeding 10 million.

q: What is the function of a 'Greenbelt' in metropolitan planning?
o: A protected ring of open space containing sprawl and preserving habitat
n: A greenbelt is a protected ring of open land encircling a city to contain sprawl and preserve natural habitat.

q: What was a common criticism of mid-20th-century Urban Renewal slum-clearance programs?
o: Demolished historic areas and displaced residents without adequate housing
n: Mid-century Urban Renewal was criticized for demolishing historic, low-income neighborhoods without providing adequate replacement housing.

q: What is 'urban blight' or 'urban decay'?
o: Converting old assets into new public amenities
Deterioration, abandonment, and economic decline of inner-city buildings
n: Urban blight/decay refers to the functional deterioration, abandonment, and economic decline of inner-city buildings and infrastructure.

q: How is residential density typically measured on planning maps?
o: Dwelling units per unit land area
n: Residential density is expressed as the number of dwelling units per unit of land area.

q: What is a 'Planned Unit Development' (PUD)?
o: A community with identical setback rules
A flexible master-planned zoning category allowing mixed uses/housing on one parcel
n: A Planned Unit Development is a flexible master-planned zoning category allowing mixed uses and housing types on one large parcel.

q: What is the fundamental difference between 'land use' and 'zoning'?
o: Land use is current activity; zoning is the legal regulation for future development
Land use is private, zoning is engineering-only
Land use is rural, zoning is urban only
n: Land use describes what is actually on the ground now; zoning is the legal regulation controlling what may be built there.

q: In Kevin Lynch's 'Image of the City', what are strategic busy focal points where paths cross called?
n: Kevin Lynch's 'nodes' are strategic, busy focal points, such as where major paths intersect.

q: What is an 'Edge' in Kevin Lynch's mental-mapping theory?
o: A linear boundary acting as a barrier or break
n: Lynch defines an 'edge' as a linear boundary that acts as a barrier or break between districts.

q: How does Kevin Lynch define a 'District'?
o: A medium-large area with a distinct identity one can mentally enter
A prominent statue at an intersection
n: Lynch's 'district' is a medium-to-large area with a distinct, shared identity a person can mentally enter.

q: What does Jane Jacobs's 'eyes on the street' concept mean for safety?
o: Windows/storefronts facing sidewalks so residents naturally watch the street
n: Jane Jacobs's 'eyes on the street' means active windows and storefronts facing the sidewalk let residents naturally watch over it.

q: What was Daniel Burnham's core philosophy for the 'City Beautiful' movement?
o: Monumental civic centers, boulevards, and classical beauty for civic pride
n: Burnham's City Beautiful movement pursued monumental civic centers, wide boulevards, and classical grandeur to inspire civic order and pride.

q: What daily schedule does Carlos Moreno's '15-Minute City' concept aim to enable?
n: Moreno's 15-Minute City aims to put daily necessities within a 15-minute walk or bike ride of home.

q: What does Patrick Geddes's 'Survey before plan' mandate?
o: Thoroughly studying a site's geography, history, culture, and people before planning
n: Geddes's 'survey before plan' calls for thoroughly studying a site's geography, history, culture, and people before laying out any plan.

q: What was the ideal destination in Ebenezer Howard's 'Three Magnets' diagram?
n: Howard's ideal 'Town-Country' magnet combined the economic opportunity of the city with the open space and nature of the countryside.

q: What threat are 'Floating City' concepts like Oceanix designed to address?
o: Rising seas and climate-driven coastal flooding
n: Floating city concepts like Oceanix are designed to protect coastal populations from rising seas and climate-driven storm flooding.

q: How did Le Corbusier map Chandigarh's sectors using a human-body analogy?
o: Capitol as 'Head', parks as 'Lungs', commerce as 'Heart'
City shaped like a skeletal arm
n: Le Corbusier mapped Chandigarh's capitol as the 'Head,' its green parks as the 'Lungs,' and its commercial center as the 'Heart.'

q: What does Kevin Lynch mean by 'urban legibility'?
o: How easily residents form a coherent mental map of a city's parts
Number of books in a library
n: Urban legibility is how easily residents can recognize and organize a city's parts into a coherent mental map.

q: Which of Doxiadis's five ekistic elements represents physical buildings that shelter people?
n: Of Doxiadis's five ekistic elements, 'Shells' are the physical buildings and structures that house people.

q: What was the typical pre-colonial layout of native Filipino barangay settlements?
o: A rigid grid around stone palaces
Linear settlements along coasts/rivers for transit and trade
n: Pre-colonial barangays typically formed linear settlements along coasts and rivers for transit, fishing, and trade.

q: What was the typical size/structure of a pre-colonial Philippine barangay?
o: A kinship community of 30-100 families led by a Datu
n: A pre-colonial barangay was a small, kinship-based community of roughly 30--100 families led by a Datu.

q: What was the goal of the Spanish 'Reducción' policy in the Philippines?
o: Grouping scattered communities into centralized towns for conversion/taxation
n: The Reducción policy resettled scattered native communities into centralized towns to ease religious conversion and tax collection.

q: What is the historic 1573 document dictating Spanish colonial town layouts called?
n: King Philip II's 1573 planning code for Spanish colonial towns is known as the Laws of the Indies.

q: Where were elite Principalia houses mandated to be built in a colonial plaza complex?
o: Facing or adjacent to the central plaza
On top of the church bell tower
n: Colonial plaza complexes required the Principalia's grand houses to face or sit adjacent to the central plaza.

q: What is the scientific definition of 'Ekistics'?
o: The multidisciplinary study of human settlements' growth and structure
n: Ekistics is the comprehensive, multidisciplinary study of human settlements and their scale, growth, and structure.

q: Which American planner designed City Beautiful master plans for Manila and Baguio in 1904?
n: Daniel Burnham visited the Philippines in 1904 to prepare City Beautiful master plans for Manila and Baguio.

q: What was the 'Parian' in Spanish colonial Manila?
o: A regulated commercial district outside Intramuros for Chinese merchants
n: The Parian was the regulated commercial district outside Intramuros's walls designated for Chinese merchants and artisans.

q: What movement inspired Quezon City's 1939 wide avenues and civic circles?
o: City Beautiful, prioritizing monumental axes and parkways
New Urbanism, focused on rural lanes
n: Quezon City's 1939 plan of wide avenues and civic circles was directly inspired by the City Beautiful movement.

q: What term did Doxiadis give to a hypothetical future single worldwide connected city?
n: Doxiadis called his hypothetical future of one continuous, planet-spanning city 'Ecumenopolis.'

q: Which Kevin Lynch element describes the channels people regularly travel along?
n: Lynch's 'paths' are the channels --- streets, walkways --- along which people habitually travel.

q: What zoning milestone did Tony Garnier's 1904 'Industrial City' concept introduce?
o: First strict separation of work and living areas
n: Tony Garnier's Cité Industrielle (1904) was among the first plans to strictly zone work areas apart from living areas.

q: Which architect wrote 'A house is a machine for living in'?
n: Le Corbusier wrote that 'a house is a machine for living in' in Vers une architecture.

q: A public building with grand columns, a pediment, and a symmetrical stone facade mimicking Greek/Roman temples is what style?
n: Grand columns, a pediment, and symmetrical stone facades echoing Greek/Roman temples define the Neoclassical style.

q: What principle is applied when benches, handles, and ceiling heights are designed to match human reach and proportion?
n: Designing fixtures and dimensions to match comfortable human reach and proportion is the principle of Human Scale.

q: What planning strategy isolates residential streets from traffic by routing it around a large block's perimeter?
n: Superblock design routes fast traffic around the perimeter of a large block, keeping the quiet residential interior free of through-traffic.

q: What was the core philosophy of the Postmodern movement emerging in the late 1960s-70s?
o: Reviving historical ornament, color, irony, and playful shapes
n: Postmodernism reintroduced historical ornament, color, irony, and playful form in reaction against strict Modernist rules.

q: What is the primary benefit of a centralized park system or greenway corridors in master planning?
o: Acting as the city's 'green lungs' for air, drainage, and recreation
n: A connected park/greenway system serves as a city's 'green lungs,' managing stormwater, air quality, and recreation.

q: What 1920s-30s style features geometric sunbursts, chevrons, and sleek metal lines, as on the Chrysler Building?
n: Geometric sunbursts, chevrons, and sleek metallic lines atop buildings like the Chrysler Building define Art Deco.

q: What proportion system uses a roughly 1:1.618 ratio found throughout nature for pleasing width-height relationships?
n: The Golden Section is the roughly 1:1.618 ratio found throughout nature and applied to pleasing architectural proportions.

q: What is the traffic-safety benefit of a cul-de-sac?
o: Eliminates fast through-traffic on residential blocks
n: A cul-de-sac's dead-end turnaround keeps fast through-traffic from cutting through quiet residential streets.

q: What road layout overlays diagonal avenues onto a rectangular grid, meeting at civic circles?
n: A Radial-Gridiron plan overlays diagonal boulevards onto a rectangular grid, meeting at civic circles or squares.

q: Which architect, nicknamed 'Queen of the Curve,' designed the Heydar Aliyev Center using digital modeling?
n: Zaha Hadid, nicknamed the 'Queen of the Curve,' designed the fluid, digitally modeled Heydar Aliyev Center.

q: What is the 'Volada' in a traditional Bahay na Bato?
o: A solid stone foundation wall sealing the ground floor
An overhanging enclosed wooden gallery on the second floor for shade and airflow
n: The volada is an overhanging, enclosed second-floor wooden gallery that shades the ground floor and allows air to circulate.
